result.title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think
result.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates language-model inference by preparing candidate continuations before the target model generates them. Its efficiency depends on how well limited drafting computation anticipates the path the target will actually follow. Anticipating this path involves two sources of uncertainty: the target model's predictions and the randomness of sampling. Yet the former requires a target-model forward pass, while the latter can be fixed before drafting. Building on this observation, we introduce DICE (Draw-Informed Candidate Selection), which pre-samples and synchronizes verification randomness across drafting and verification. By combining these known draws with predictions from an existing drafter, DICE allocates computation toward continuations more likely to be used in the current sampling run. This principle guides node selection throughout draft-tree construction and extends to asynchronous prefetching, where DICE predicts which next-round drafts to prepare. Without additional drafter training or changes to the target sampling distribution, DICE achieves state-of-the-art decoding throughput across diverse settings, with speedups of up to 24.6pp over strong baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DICE：在投机解码中预先采样并与验证阶段同步随机数，使 drafter 结合已知采样结果，把候选树构建与异步预取的计算集中到当前采样运行更可能采用的续写上，从而提升解码吞吐。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用受限草稿计算预判目标路径并定向分配计算」的构想，可能与 LVR 中动态计算预算、候选分支筛选及预测式预取有概念联系，但对象是 token 级加速而非推理状态，可供核查迁移价值。
